'''Laura Grace DeMarco''' is an American mathematician who is a professor of mathematics at [[Harvard University]], whose research concerns [[dynamical system]]s and [[complex analysis]].<ref>[http://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/ Laura DeMarco Home Page at Harvard]</ref>

== Career ==
DeMarco received her Ph.D. from [[Harvard University]] in 2002 under the supervision of [[Curtis T. McMullen]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=69493|title=Laura DeMarco}}</ref> She held an NSF Postdoctoral Fellowship and was an L. E. Dickson Instructor at the [[University of Chicago]] from September 2002 to August 2005. She was also an assistant professor at the [[University of Chicago]], and then she moved to the [[University of Illinois at Chicago]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Laura DeMarco|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/laura-g-demarco-r4snls/|access-date=2020-11-06|website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref> where she was tenured and promoted to professor. She moved to [[Northwestern University]] in 2014,<ref>{{Cite journal|title=2017 Ruth Lyttle Satter Prize|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201704/rnoti-p316.pdf|journal=Notices of the AMS|volume=64|pages=316}}</ref> and was promoted to Henry S. Noyes Professor of Mathematics in 2019, before she moved to [[Harvard University]] in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-06-23|title=Math Department announces three new faculty members|url=https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2020/06/math-department-announces-three-new-faculty-members/|access-date=2020-08-12|website=Harvard Gazette|language=en-US}}</ref> She has been appointed the [[Hollis Chair of Mathematicks and Natural Philosophy|Hollis Professor of Mathematicks and Natural Philosophy]] as of 2026 <ref>https://www.math.harvard.edu/laura-demarco-appointed-hollis-professor-of-mathematicks-and-natural-philosophy/</ref>

DeMarco is an organizer of GROW (Graduate Research Opportunities for Women) [[undergraduate]] conference.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Graduate Research Opportunities for Women 2020 {{!}} Department of Mathematics {{!}} The University of Chicago|url=https://mathematics.uchicago.edu/grow2020/|access-date=2020-10-27|website=mathematics.uchicago.edu}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
In 2013, DeMarco became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in the inaugural class of fellows.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]</ref> In 2017, she received the AMS [[Ruth Lyttle Satter Prize in Mathematics]] in Mathematics for her contributions to [[complex dynamics]], [[potential theory]], and the emerging field of [[arithmetic dynamics]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=3222 Ruth Lyttle Satter Prize 2017]</ref> In 2020, DeMarco was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=NAS Election 2020|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2020-nas-election.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200428010617/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2020-nas-election.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 28, 2020}}</ref>

She was an invited speaker at the 2018 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], speaking in the section on [[Dynamical system|Dynamical Systems]] and Ordinary Differential Equations.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.icm2018.org/portal/en/icm-speakers|title=Speakers|work=ICM 2018|access-date=2018-02-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171215001530/http://www.icm2018.org/portal/en/icm-speakers|archive-date=2017-12-15|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{YouTube|HClk4YiDRns}}</ref> She is the 2023 [[Noether Lecture|AWM-AMS Emmy Noether Lecturer]] in recognition of her "fundamental and influential contributions to complex dynamics, arithmetic dynamics, and arithmetic geometry."<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 AWM-AMS Emmy Noether Lecture |date=26 April 2022 |url=https://awm-math.org/2023-awm-ams-emmy-noether-lecture/}}</ref>

Her work with [[Holly Krieger]] and Hexi Ye, "Uniform Manin–Mumford for a family of genus 2 curves", published in the ''[[Annals of Mathematics]]'', won the 2020 Alexanderson Award of the [[American Institute of Mathematics]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://aimath.org/anderson-award-2020/|title=Alexanderson Award 2020|publisher=American Institute of Mathematics|access-date=November 17, 2020}}</ref>

==Research==
DeMarco's research involves algebraic, [[arithmetic dynamics|arithmetic]] and [[complex dynamics]] with an emphasis on their interactions with each other. She has studied dynamically meaningful [[Compactification (mathematics)|compactifications]] of the [[moduli space]] of [[Rational function|rational maps]] on <math>\mathbb{P}^1.</math> <ref>{{cite journal|journal=Duke Mathematical Journal |title=Iteration at the boundary of the pace of rational maps|issue=130|year=2005|pages=607–637}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|journal=Journal of the American Mathematical Society|title=The moduli space of quadratic rational maps|issue=20|year=2007|pages=321–355}}</ref> In joint work with [[Curtis McMullen]], she showed how [[Simplicial complex|simplicial]] [[Metric space|metrized]] [[Tree (graph theory)|trees]] can be used to compactify the moduli space of [[polynomials]].<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Annales Scientifique de l'ENS |title=Trees and the dynamics of polynomials|issue=41|year=2008|pages=337–383}}</ref> Together with Xander Faber, DeMarco has studied degenerations of complex dynamical systems from the viewpoint of [[Berkovich space]]s.<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Forum of Mathematics Sigma |title=Degenerations of Complex Dynamical Systems|issue=2|year=2014|page=36}}</ref>

With Matthew Baker, DeMarco pioneered the study of [[Zilber-Pink conjecture|unlikely intersections]] in arithmetic dynamics <ref>{{cite journal|journal=Duke Mathematical Journal|title=Preperiodic points and unlikely intersections|issue=159(1)|year=2011|pages=1–29}}</ref>  and formulated the dynamical [[André-Oort conjecture]].<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Forum of Mathematics Pi|title=Special curves and post-critically finite curves|issue=1|year=2013|page=35}}</ref> Together with [[Holly Krieger]] and Hexi Ye, DeMarco proved the first instances of the uniform dynamical [[Manin-Mumford conjecture]] for [[Lattès map]]s<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Annals of Mathematics |title=Uniform Manin-Mumford for a family of genus 2 curves|issue=191(3)|year=2020|pages=949–1001}}</ref> and for [[Complex quadratic polynomial|quadratic unicritical polynomials]].<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Journal of Modern Dynamics |title=Common preperiodic points for quadratic polynomials|issue=18|year=2022|pages=363–413}}</ref> In collaboration with Niki Myrto Mavraki, DeMarco studied the notion of non-degeneracy for polarized dynamical systems and its relation to stability.<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Compositio Mathematica |title=Dynamics on <math>\mathbb{P}^1</math>: preperiodic points and pairwise stability|issue=160(2)|year=2024|pages=356–387}}</ref> Later with Niki Myrto Mavraki and Hexi Ye, DeMarco proved a uniform version of the dynamical André-Oort conjecture.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bounded geometry for PCF-special subvarieties|year=2024|url=https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.17343}}</ref>
